name: Dust ring breaks down a score
looks: A percentage sits at the centre of a ring made of hundreds of tiny dots rather than a stroke; the dots are coloured in two or three bands around the ring's circumference, each band's arc length matching its share. A short legend below lists each category with its colour swatch and raw count, settling a beat after the ring itself.
build: Bucket dots by category and lay each bucket along its own arc, angle = category.count/total * 2*PI, with 1-2px radius jitter per dot so the ring reads as dust rather than a clean stroke. The centre percentage count-up ties to the same clock. Legend rows clip in from the left on a short stagger after the ring settles, swatch dot first, then label, then count.
sound: A soft granular patter as the ring's dots settle into their bands, a rising tone under the centre percentage, a light tick per legend row.
prompt: Build a ring out of many small dots instead of a drawn stroke, colouring bands of the ring by category so each arc's length shows its share of the whole, with the overall score counting up in the centre. Settle a short legend underneath a beat later, one row per category with its colour and raw count.
